requirements.requirement: Inventory application exists on node2 and produces log messages
requirements.summary: No pre-existing inventory application was found on node2 (cmd-6d0d72ff200342e5), so a minimal systemd-managed inventory.service was created (/usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh + unit, enabled and active) emitting tagged local0.info log lines via logger, confirmed present in /var/log/syslog.

requirements.requirement: node2 forwards inventory log messages to a centralized collector on node1
requirements.summary: rsyslog on node1 was configured with imtcp on port 10514 and a dynaFile per-host template; node2 was configured with omfwd TCP forwarding of local0.* traffic with a disk-assisted queue. A manual marker message logged on node2 was observed arriving in node1's collector output, directly confirming end-to-end delivery.

requirements.requirement: Received messages persisted under /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
requirements.summary: The /var/log/inventory directory was created on node1 with appropriate ownership, and node2.log was populated by the dynaFile template containing the forwarded inventory log lines, directly observed via ls/grep on node1.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node1 restarts
requirements.summary: A healthy baseline (boot_id bdd5de93..., active rsyslog, 4-line log) was captured, node1 was natively rebooted, a connection timeout directly confirmed disruption, then a new boot_id (02df6e21...) confirmed the restart, rsyslog was observed auto-active/enabled with the listener rebound and the prior log file intact, and a fresh post-restart marker sent from node2 was confirmed delivered into node2.log — a complete baseline-disruption-recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node2 restarts
requirements.summary: A healthy baseline (boot_id dfeb3b70..., active rsyslog/inventory services) was captured, node2 was natively rebooted, a connection timeout directly confirmed disruption, then a new boot_id (4ba54a48...) confirmed the restart, inventory.service and rsyslog were observed auto-active/enabled, and a fresh post-restart marker logged on node2 was confirmed delivered and persisted in node1's node2.log — a complete baseline-disruption-recovery transition.

overall_summary: All five material outcomes of the task — an inventory application on node2 producing logs, TCP forwarding to node1, persistence at /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and log-flow continuity across independent restarts of both node1 and node2 — are directly supported by observed command evidence showing full baseline-disruption-recovery transitions with changed boot IDs and confirmed post-restart message delivery. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is satisfied by the same restart sequences, and the fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the final boot IDs on both nodes with no contradictory findings. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: The captured evidence relies on the executor's own bounded command outputs (grep/tail snippets) rather than a full independent audit of rsyslog internal queue state, so subtle edge-case forwarding failures (e.g., under sustained network partition rather than a full reboot) are not directly tested.

No sample of continuously-generated (non-marker) inventory log lines spanning a longer duration was captured, so long-run reliability of the 5-second-interval logger loop is inferred rather than exhaustively observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing all state-changing commands chronologically: creation of the inventory app script/service (cmd-14d3476927984c55, corrected by cmd-8b76297ba0d74f94 after a POSIX-sh $RANDOM incompatibility was noticed — a minor, immediately-corrected iteration, not residue), systemd unit creation (cmd-4194749f4e8e4a42), the /var/log/inventory directory (cmd-2e4167229c2a4f52), rsyslog configs on both nodes plus the /var/spool/rsyslog queue directory (cmd-9402e322e68f402f, cmd-c7b721d12e7a4d96), and the two reboots (cmd-b108f5594c3a424b, cmd-fa79f9868db64e21). Every mutation maps directly to a material requirement or its restart-evidence collection; manual marker messages (cmd-83695a517aa7440a, cmd-56606e74136d4769, cmd-f4d0fd6dcebb4113) are low-risk verification writes to the application's own log stream. The fixed lifecycle snapshots show no failed services, no unexpected package-health issues, and only expected boot-cycle systemd-private temp directories before/after — no abandoned files or unnecessary residue was found.
